title: Texas's 12th Congressional District General Election, 2026
description: The general election for Texas's 12th Congressional District features first-term incumbent Republican Craig Goldman facing Democratic nominee Angela "Heli" Rodriguez Prilliman. The district covers parts of Tarrant and Parker Counties in the Fort Worth area and was redrawn under new maps passed in August 2025, which were challenged in court but ultimately upheld by the U.S. Supreme Court. Cook Political Report rates the race as Solid Republican, with a PVI of R+11; the district backed Donald Trump by 24 points in 2024. Goldman, a former Texas House Majority Leader, is running on his conservative record on border security, tax cuts, and national defense, while Rodriguez Prilliman, a tech entrepreneur and progressive activist, is campaigning on universal healthcare, affordable childcare, and removing billionaire money from politics.
polling_note: No district-level polls specific to Texas's 12th Congressional District were found for this election cycle. Statewide generic ballot polls show a competitive environment but are not disaggregated by district.

candidates.name: Craig Goldman
candidates.summary: Craig Goldman is the incumbent U.S. Representative for Texas's 12th Congressional District, first elected in 2024. He previously served 12 years in the Texas House of Representatives, where he was Majority Leader and chaired the Energy Resources Committee. Goldman serves on the House Energy and Commerce Committee and emphasizes conservative positions on border security, tax reduction, and national defense.

candidates.name: Angela "Heli" Rodriguez Prilliman
candidates.summary: Angela "Heli" Rodriguez Prilliman is a progressive Democratic candidate and the nominee for Texas's 12th Congressional District. She is a tech entrepreneur, founder of Lacquerbar and Lacquerbar U, and a graduate of Texas A&M University. Rodriguez Prilliman previously ran for the U.S. Senate in 2024 and won the 2026 Democratic primary for this House seat with 59.8% of the vote. Her campaign focuses on universal healthcare, a $10/day cap on childcare, voting rights, and removing corporate money from politics.

forecast.rationale: No district-level polling exists, reducing quantitative confidence. However, race fundamentals strongly favor Republicans: incumbent Craig Goldman holds the seat; Cook Political Report rates it Solid Republican; the district has a PVI of R+11 and backed Trump by 24 points in 2024. The district was redrawn under new 2025 maps that were challenged but upheld by the Supreme Court, though the provided data does not indicate a material shift in the district's partisan lean. Rodriguez Prilliman is a credible Democratic nominee who won her primary with 59.8%, but there is no district-specific evidence of a competitive race. The safe Republican rating reflects the overwhelming structural advantage in this district.
